basics.name: Stefan Stepanovic
basics.label: Senior Research Engineer
basics.summary: Senior research engineer with 5+ years in industrial R&D, at the intersection of geometry, optimization and learning. Has taken 3D reconstruction systems from research to shipped product, across large-scale structure from motion, neural rendering and Gaussian Splatting. Currently exploring agents that reason over real-world scenes and the generation of large, unbounded ones.

projects.name: Structure from motion and 3D reconstruction
highlights: Designed and maintain the company's proprietary SfM pipeline. It scales from single objects and indoor spaces to multiple city blocks or 12 km of road, and reconstructs 60k images in 3D in under a day on a single consumer-level machine.
Extended it to a wide range of industrial and commercial cameras and 3D scanners, across driving, handheld, aerial, drone and mixed captures.
Scaled bundle adjustment with clustering algorithms and GPU-based solvers, which made SfM an order of magnitude faster.
Made the classical pipeline more robust with deep learning: learned mapping, camera calibration, gravity alignment and depth estimation.

projects.name: Neural rendering and Gaussian Splatting
highlights: Built the company's real-time neural rendering system from scratch, with photorealistic renders of captured scenes in HD at 30 FPS. Shipped the first MVP to a customer.
Integrated it into Unreal Engine as a plugin with streaming to mobile devices, and delivered the first public demo of the technology on captures of Seattle.

Improved Gaussian Splatting rendering of views far from the captured ones, by distilling corrections from generative image and video models. Also researched densification strategies, both published and proprietary.

projects.name: Scene understanding and spatial intelligence
highlights: Brought semantic understanding to reconstructed 3D scenes and shipped open-vocabulary segmentation as a product feature.
Working on R&D for the company's spatial intelligence product: AI agents that reason over captured 3D scenes. Prototyped and showcased it on a scan of a residential home under construction.

projects.name: Mentorship and hiring
highlights: Designed the assignments and conducted the interviews for four intern hiring rounds.

Defined and supervised four research internships across neural rendering and Gaussian Splatting. One, a six-month project on generative 3D diffusion models, was run as a research collaboration with international 3D experts.

projects.name: Customer and product work
highlights: Made the C++ pipeline releasable as a product, with Python bindings, Docker packaging and internal quality metrics.
Work directly with customers: support and feature planning for existing ones, tailored demos for prospective ones.

Co-led the company's exhibition at INTERGEO 2026, the leading geospatial conference: presented the product line to industry attendees and assessed market demand for 3D reconstruction and spatial intelligence.

work.name: École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
work.position: Research Fellow, Visual Intelligence Lab (Prof. Amir Zamir)

projects.name: Multi-task representation learning
highlights: Researched representations shared across many vision tasks, such as depth, surface normals and segmentation, learned by a single network.
Developed loss-weighting methods that balanced training across tasks, giving stable training and consistent results on every task.
Designed a dropout-based regularization that orders the learned representation from coarse to fine, similar to PCA, so detail can be controlled directly in the representation.

projects.name: Structure from motion
highlights: Optimized the SfM mapping pipeline for long driving captures used in HD mapping for self-driving.
Researched and delivered point-free SfM based on general 3D curves, which works even in texture-poor areas.
